topic: Hilbert considers how six previously listed properties of invariants imply one another, then begins stating a general theorem about systems of rational functions and integral rational functions in variables x_1,...,x_n that he wants to prove.

triage.modern_statement: The note can't be fully pinned down. Hilbert says that properties 1, 2 and 6 in a list of six properties of invariants (or of systems of invariants) on an earlier page probably always follow from property 4. Page [112] doesn't say what those properties are, so the implication can't be written as an exact modern statement. The context suggests the question belongs to Hilbert's finiteness questions for invariants. On the same page he starts stating a general theorem about systems of rational functions and integral rational (polynomial) functions in x_1,...,x_n. That matches the setting of what later became Hilbert's 14th Problem: if K is a subfield of k(x_1,...,x_n), is the algebra K ∩ k[x_1,...,x_n] finitely generated over k? This link to the 14th Problem is my inference and is not confirmed by the note.
triage.answered_by: The exact implication can't be traced without the list of six properties. If the note does belong to the finite-generation question (my inference, not confirmed), the general form Hilbert later posed as Problem 14 (1900) was shown to be false by Masayoshi Nagata's counterexample (1959). Nagata built a linear action of a non-reductive group whose ring of invariants is not finitely generated.

evidence.claim: Hilbert's 14th Problem concerns the k-algebra R = K ∩ k[x_1,...,x_n], where K is a subfield of k(x_1,...,x_n). Hilbert conjectured that all such algebras are finitely generated over k. This is the same setting of rational functions and integral rational functions that the page describes.
Nagata gave a counterexample. He built a linear action of an algebraic (non-reductive) group G for which K[x_1,...,x_n]^G is not finitely generated, which settles the 14th Problem negatively.
Work on finite generation questions related to the 14th Problem continues in recent literature, for example on graded linear series.
Related finiteness questions are still studied for the rings of constants of polynomial derivations.

triage.why: The note only refers to properties 1, 2, 4 and 6 by number, and they are defined on an earlier page that wasn't provided. So the specific implication can't be identified, checked or traced in the literature. The surrounding material about systems of rational and polynomial functions points to the finite-generation question that became Hilbert's 14th Problem. That problem was answered negatively by Nagata in 1959, and related finite-generation questions are still studied. Still, it can't be shown that this note is that problem or a precursor of it, so whether the note's own question is an active research topic remains unclear.
